root_cause_analysis.mechanism: In COCO, American-style pickup trucks (e.g. Ford F-150) were frequently annotated as 'truck', while smaller compact utility pickups were annotated as 'car'. In Indian traffic (UVH-26), Mahindra Bolero pickups and Tata Ace mini-trucks share high visual similarity with SUVs and passenger vans.
root_cause_analysis.mitigation: Exclude ambiguous LCVs from primary car/truck definitions and enforce canonical mapping: heavy commercial lorries -> truck, standard passenger vehicles -> car.

root_cause_analysis.mechanism: Trucks in background traffic occupy small bounding box areas (<0.5% of 1080p frame) with low pixel contrast, causing high false-negative rate at standard confidence thresholds.
root_cause_analysis.mitigation: Incorporate multi-scale training with random scaling (scale=0.6) and VisDrone steep-angle surveillance examples.

root_cause_analysis.error_modality: Perspective Distortion between CCTV and Street Driving
root_cause_analysis.mechanism: Surveillance cameras mounted 5-10 meters above intersections view truck roofs and cargo bays rather than the front grilles typical of dashcam or pedestrian photography.
root_cause_analysis.mitigation: Train directly on UVH-26 high-angle Bengaluru Safe City CCTV imagery to learn overhead roof and cargo bed features.

root_cause_analysis.error_modality: Class Imbalance in Primary Training Corpus
root_cause_analysis.mechanism: In earlier baseline, cars outnumbered trucks 3:1 (3,580 cars vs 1,284 trucks), causing the network cross-entropy loss to favor car predictions on ambiguous vehicle boundaries.
root_cause_analysis.mitigation: Targeted truck oversampling (1.5x) and HSV value augmentation in Experiment D to equalize gradient contributions.
